<issue identifier="MM-505">
<title>Enforce the advertised PAR-only authorization flow at /oauth/authorize</title>
<description>
Our authorization-server metadata advertises `require_pushed_authorization_requests: true` and (since PR #517) `require_request_uri_registration: true`, but `resolve_authorize_params` in `crates/pds/src/routes/oauth_authorize.rs` still accepts a direct (non-PAR) `GET /oauth/authorize` with inline parameters, and `GetAuthorizationQuery` silently ignores a JAR `request` parameter we advertise as unsupported (`request_parameter_supported: false`). The atproto OAuth profile mandates PAR; the reference provider rejects non-PAR authorize requests.

Scope:

* Reject direct authorization requests that arrive without a PAR-issued `request_uri` (spec-correct error page / `invalid_request`), keeping the wallet/consent paths working.
* Reject requests carrying a `request` (JAR) parameter rather than silently dropping it.
* Conformance-suite coverage for both rejections.

**Sequencing gate — do not start until the gap-12 verification passes.** [pckt.blog](<http://pckt.blog>) currently reaches us via the direct-authorize fallback; enforcement before their metadata cache picks up PR #517's `request_uri` capability fields would turn their silent post-consent failure into a hard failure at flow start. First confirm (per the addendum in `docs/2026-08-03-oauth-interop-audit.md`) that pckt's redirect for an obsign-hosted handle carries `request_uri=`, then enforce.

Context: gap identified in the 2026-08-03 OAuth interop audit ("we accept despite advertising require_pushed_authorization_requests: true"), re-raised by review on PR #517.
</description>
<team name="Mal's Machinations"/>
<label>Wave 2: Auth</label>
<label>Security</label>
<project name="ezpds">An easy-to-host PDS on the ATProtocol, MacOS. Grandma-approved.</project>
</issue>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**

183	## Addendum (2026-08-12): pckt.blog root cause — gap 12, absent `request_uri` capability fields
184	
185	The instrumented repro (item 7) landed and the pckt.blog failure is fully explained. It was
186	never the callback redirect: a HAR of the real flow plus controlled curl probes against
187	pckt's own endpoints showed their Laravel backend *receives* our `code`+`state`+`iss`
188	callback with a live session, passes its state check (wrong/absent state 403s; the real flow
189	302s with a "couldn't complete the login" flash), then fails locally in ~100 ms without ever
190	contacting our token endpoint.
191	
192	The discriminating experiment: pckt uses **PAR** against bsky.social *and* against a
193	third-party self-hosted reference PDS (pds.robocracy.org) — but silently downgrades to a
194	legacy direct-authorize flow against us, for did:plc and did:web accounts alike. The one
195	relevant metadata difference: the reference provider emits `request_uri_parameter_supported`,
196	`require_request_uri_registration`, and `request_parameter_supported` explicitly, and we
197	emitted none of them. OpenID Connect Discovery §3 (which defines all three fields) defaults
198	`request_uri_parameter_supported` to `true` when absent — and the atproto profile pins
199	`require_request_uri_registration`'s default to `true` and forbids `false` — but pckt's
200	client reads absence as "legacy server without PAR" and takes a fallback path whose callback
201	half is broken (their bug — but absence is indistinguishable from incapability to such
202	clients). Beacon remains unexplained (still zero server contact).
203	
204	Fix: emit the three fields explicitly (`request_uri_parameter_supported: true`,
205	`require_request_uri_registration: true`, and — honestly, diverging from the reference —
206	`request_parameter_supported: false`, since we do not implement JAR). Conformance suite pins
207	their presence. The suites only prove serialization — they cannot prove a deployed client
208	*selects* PAR — so the live probe is the release gate for this item: after the production
209	deploy, start pckt's flow for an obsign-hosted handle and check the redirect URL for
210	`request_uri=` (PAR path) instead of inline `state`/`code_challenge` (legacy path), and
211	record the outcome here before closing the pckt.blog item. If pckt still downgrades, the
212	next lever is their gate possibly requiring `request_parameter_supported: true`, which we

## Addendum (2026-08-12): pckt.blog root cause — gap 12, absent `request_uri` capability fields

The instrumented repro (item 7) landed and the pckt.blog failure is fully explained. It was
never the callback redirect: a HAR of the real flow plus controlled curl probes against
pckt's own endpoints showed their Laravel backend *receives* our `code`+`state`+`iss`
callback with a live session, passes its state check (wrong/absent state 403s; the real flow
302s with a "couldn't complete the login" flash), then fails locally in ~100 ms without ever
contacting our token endpoint.

The discriminating experiment: pckt uses **PAR** against bsky.social *and* against a
third-party self-hosted reference PDS (pds.robocracy.org) — but silently downgrades to a
legacy direct-authorize flow against us, for did:plc and did:web accounts alike. The one
relevant metadata difference: the reference provider emits `request_uri_parameter_supported`,
`require_request_uri_registration`, and `request_parameter_supported` explicitly, and we
emitted none of them. OpenID Connect Discovery §3 (which defines all three fields) defaults
`request_uri_parameter_supported` to `true` when absent — and the atproto profile pins
`require_request_uri_registration`'s default to `true` and forbids `false` — but pckt's
client reads absence as "legacy server without PAR" and takes a fallback path whose callback
half is broken (their bug — but absence is indistinguishable from incapability to such
clients). Beacon remains unexplained (still zero server contact).

Fix: emit the three fields explicitly (`request_uri_parameter_supported: true`,
`require_request_uri_registration: true`, and — honestly, diverging from the reference —
`request_parameter_supported: false`, since we do not implement JAR). Conformance suite pins
their presence. The suites only prove serialization — they cannot prove a deployed client
*selects* PAR — so the live probe is the release gate for this item: after the production
deploy, start pckt's flow for an obsign-hosted handle and check the redirect URL for
`request_uri=` (PAR path) instead of inline `state`/`code_challenge` (legacy path), and
record the outcome here before closing the pckt.blog item. If pckt still downgrades, the
next lever is their gate possibly requiring `request_parameter_supported: true`, which we
should not lie about — that would mean implementing JAR or contacting pckt.

5	// Processes:

7	//   POST: validates client + redirect_uri first → handles deny/approve → generates auth code

12	//! `GET`/`POST /oauth/authorize` — the authorization endpoint and its consent page.
13	//!
14	//! **Non-PAR requests resolve live.** A cache miss on a URL-shaped `client_id` fetches the
15	//! client-metadata document with the same resolver PAR uses (`auth/oauth_client_resolution.rs`),
16	//! so direct authorization requests from real-world clients that skip PAR (bsky.social tolerates
17	//! them) still work; the document is cached only after the request fully validates. The
18	//! reverse-FQDN private-use-redirect rule is enforced here as well as at PAR.
19	//!
20	//! **`response_mode`.** Honored on every success and error redirect: `query` (the default) or
21	//! `fragment` (the `@atproto/oauth-client-browser` default).
22	//!
23	//! **Push dispatch (Phase C).** The GET's wallet path owns `dispatch_login_approval_push`: a
24	//! `login_hint` naming a hosted account gets a sealed `login-approval` push via
25	//! `notifications::notify_device`. The hint is resolved with local lookups only — never outbound
26	//! resolution, because it is attacker-suppliable on an unauthenticated surface — and the
27	//! two-digit match code (the V060 `match_code` column) is latched and shown on the page only
28	//! when a device was actually enqueued.

163	/// Distinguishes client-caused failures from server-caused failures in PAR resolution.
164	///

166	/// request-didn't-work page, infrastructure failures (which should trigger alerts)
167	/// get the server-error page. Both variants carry finished user-register copy; the
168	/// mechanical detail lives in the tracing at the failure site.
169	enum ResolveError {
170	    /// The client sent an invalid or expired `request_uri`, or a mismatched `client_id`.
171	    Client(&'static str),
172	    /// A database or deserialization failure prevented resolution.
173	    Server(&'static str),
174	}

176	/// Shared error-page copy for infrastructure failures. The mechanical cause is already
177	/// traced at the failure site, so the user's sentence carries none of it.
178	const SERVER_ERROR_PAGE_MSG: &str = "This server hit a problem before it could finish. \
179	     Nothing was granted. Wait a moment, then start the sign-in again from the app.";
180	
181	/// Shared error-page copy for a request naming a response delivery mode this server
182	/// doesn't support. The `response_mode` detail goes to the log, not the user's sentence.
183	const UNSUPPORTED_RESPONSE_MODE_MSG: &str = "The app asked for a kind of sign-in response \
184	     this server doesn't support, so the request stopped here. Nothing was granted. If \
185	     this keeps happening, the problem is on the app's side.";

187	/// Resolve `GetAuthorizationQuery` into a fully-populated `AuthorizeQuery`.
188	///
189	/// When `request_uri` is present (PAR flow), atomically consumes the stored request
190	/// (single-use per RFC 9126 §4), deserializes the params JSON, and validates `client_id`
191	/// matches. When absent (direct flow), constructs `AuthorizeQuery` from raw params.
192	async fn resolve_authorize_params(
193	    state: &AppState,
194	    raw: GetAuthorizationQuery,
195	) -> Result<AuthorizeQuery, ResolveError> {
196	    if let Some(uri) = raw.request_uri {
197	        let row = match consume_par_request(&state.db, &uri).await {
198	            Ok(Some(r)) => r,
199	            Ok(None) => {
200	                return Err(ResolveError::Client(
201	                    "This sign-in link has expired or was already used. Nothing was \
202	                     granted. Go back to the app and start the sign-in again.",
203	                ))
204	            }
205	            Err(e) => {
206	                tracing::error!(error = %e, "db error consuming PAR request");
207	                return Err(ResolveError::Server(SERVER_ERROR_PAGE_MSG));
208	            }
209	        };
210	
211	        if row.client_id != raw.client_id {
212	            tracing::info!(
213	                client_id = %raw.client_id,
214	                "authorize request rejected: client_id does not match the pushed authorization request"
215	            );
216	            return Err(ResolveError::Client(
217	                "This sign-in request doesn't match the app that started it, so it \
218	                 stopped here. Nothing was granted. Go back to the app and start the \
219	                 sign-in again.",
220	            ));
221	        }

223	        let stored: StoredPARParams = match serde_json::from_str(&row.request_parameters) {
224	            Ok(p) => p,
225	            Err(e) => {
226	                tracing::error!(
227	                    client_id = %raw.client_id,
228	                    error = %e,
229	                    "failed to deserialize stored PAR request parameters; possible schema drift or DB corruption"
230	                );
231	                return Err(ResolveError::Server(SERVER_ERROR_PAGE_MSG));
232	            }
233	        };
234	
235	        // The PAR endpoint validated the mode before storing it, so a parse failure here
236	        // means the stored row was hand-edited or the schema drifted — a client error is
237	        // still the safer framing (nothing redirects yet).
238	        let response_mode =
239	            ResponseMode::parse(Some(stored.response_mode.as_str())).map_err(|desc| {

258	        // unknown mode here — before any redirect is issued — matches the PAR posture.

300	    /// A private-use-scheme `redirect_uri` whose scheme is not the client_id host's
301	    /// reverse-FQDN. Carries the rule text naming the required scheme.
302	    PrivateUseRedirectMismatch(String),
303	}

305	/// Look up the registered client, parse its metadata, and validate `redirect_uri`.
306	///
307	/// Shared by both the GET and POST authorization handlers, which must confirm the
308	/// client and redirect target are safe before issuing any redirect. Returns the
309	/// parsed [`ClientMetadata`] on success, or a [`ClientValidationError`] the caller
310	/// renders as its own error page.
311	///
312	/// A cache miss for a URL-shaped `client_id` resolves the client's metadata document
313	/// live (the same ATProto resolver `/oauth/par` uses). PAR normally does this first —
314	/// but not every real client uses PAR (bsky.social tolerates direct authorization
315	/// requests, so non-PAR clients exist in the wild), and without this branch such a
316	/// client dies here with "not registered" despite publishing valid metadata. The
317	/// fetched document is cached only after the whole request validates, mirroring PAR's
318	/// rejected-requests-must-not-plant-rows doctrine.
319	async fn lookup_and_validate_client(
320	    state: &AppState,
321	    client_id: &str,
322	    redirect_uri: &str,
323	) -> Result<ClientMetadata, ClientValidationError> {
324	    let (client_metadata_json, freshly_fetched) = match get_oauth_client(&state.db, client_id).await
325	    {
326	        Ok(Some(row)) => (row.client_metadata, false),
327	        Ok(None) if client_id.starts_with("https://") || client_id.starts_with("http://") => {
328	            match crate::auth::oauth_client_resolution::resolve_client_metadata(
329	                &state.http_client,
330	                client_id,
331	            )
332	            .await
333	            {
334	                Ok(json) => (json, true),
335	                Err(e) => {
336	                    tracing::info!(client_id = %client_id, error = %e, "URL client_id resolution failed at authorize");
337	                    return Err(ClientValidationError::ResolutionFailed(e.to_string()));
338	                }
339	            }
340	        }
341	        Ok(None) => return Err(ClientValidationError::UnknownClient),
342	        Err(e) => {
343	            tracing::error!(error = %e, "db error looking up OAuth client");
344	            return Err(ClientValidationError::DbError);
345	        }
346	    };
347	
348	    let metadata: ClientMetadata = match serde_json::from_str(&client_metadata_json) {
349	        Ok(m) => m,
350	        Err(e) => {
351	            tracing::error!(
352	                client_id = %client_id,
353	                error = %e,
354	                "failed to parse OAuth client metadata"
355	            );
356	            return Err(ClientValidationError::MalformedMetadata);
357	        }
358	    };
359	
360	    if !metadata.redirect_uris.contains(&redirect_uri.to_string()) {
361	        return Err(ClientValidationError::InvalidRedirectUri);
362	    }
363	
364	    // The reverse-FQDN rule for private-use-scheme redirects, enforced here as well as
365	    // at PAR so the direct (non-PAR) flow can't sidestep it.
366	    if let Err(desc) =
367	        crate::auth::oauth_client_resolution::validate_private_use_redirect(client_id, redirect_uri)
368	    {
369	        return Err(ClientValidationError::PrivateUseRedirectMismatch(desc));
370	    }
371	
372	    // Cache a freshly resolved document only after the request fully validated, so a
373	    // rejected request never plants a client row.
374	    if freshly_fetched {
375	        if let Err(e) = upsert_oauth_client(&state.db, client_id, &client_metadata_json).await {
376	            tracing::error!(error = %e, client_id = %client_id, "failed to cache resolved OAuth client metadata");
377	            return Err(ClientValidationError::DbError);
378	        }
379	    }
380	
381	    Ok(metadata)
382	}

384	/// `GET /oauth/authorize` — validate request parameters and render the consent page.
385	///
386	/// Accepts either direct query parameters or a PAR `request_uri` (RFC 9126).
387	/// Returns an HTML error page (400) for errors that make a redirect unsafe:
388	/// unknown `client_id` or mismatched `redirect_uri`. All other parameter errors
389	/// redirect to `redirect_uri` with an `error` query parameter per RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1.
390	pub async fn get_authorization(
391	    State(state): State<AppState>,
392	    headers: HeaderMap,
393	    Query(raw): Query<GetAuthorizationQuery>,
394	) -> Response {
395	    // RFC 9207 issuer identifier, emitted as `iss` on every authorization response.
396	    // Trailing slash trimmed to match the AS-metadata `issuer` value exactly.
397	    let issuer = state.config.public_url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
398	    let params = match resolve_authorize_params(&state, raw).await {
399	        Ok(p) => p,
400	        Err(ResolveError::Client(msg)) => {
401	            return error_page("This sign-in request didn't work", msg).into_response()
402	        }
403	        Err(ResolveError::Server(msg)) => {
404	            return error_page("Something went wrong on this server", msg).into_response()
405	        }
406	    };
407	
408	    // Client and redirect_uri must be validated before any redirect is issued.
409	    let metadata =
410	        match lookup_and_validate_client(&state, &params.client_id, &params.redirect_uri).await {
411	            Ok(m) => m,
412	            Err(ClientValidationError::UnknownClient) => {
413	                return error_page(
414	                    "This app isn't recognized",
415	                    "This server doesn't recognize the app asking to sign you in, so \
416	                     the request stopped here. Nothing was granted. If this keeps \
417	                     happening, the problem is on the app's side.",
418	                )
419	                .into_response()
420	            }
421	            Err(ClientValidationError::ResolutionFailed(desc)) => {
422	                return error_page(
423	                    "This app isn't recognized",
424	                    &format!(
425	                        "This server couldn't verify the app asking to sign you in, so \
426	                         the request stopped here. Nothing was granted. Details for the \
427	                         app's developer: {desc}"
428	                    ),
429	                )
430	                .into_response()
431	            }
432	            Err(ClientValidationError::PrivateUseRedirectMismatch(desc)) => {
433	                return error_page(
434	                    "Can't return you to the app",
435	                    &format!(
436	                        "The app asked to send you to an address it hasn't registered, \
437	                         so you weren't sent anywhere and nothing was granted. Details \
438	                         for the app's developer: {desc}"
439	                    ),
440	                )
441	                .into_response()
442	            }
443	            Err(ClientValidationError::DbError) => {
444	                return error_page("Something went wrong on this server", SERVER_ERROR_PAGE_MSG)
445	                    .into_response()
446	            }
447	            Err(ClientValidationError::MalformedMetadata) => {
448	                return error_page(
449	                    "This app is set up incorrectly",
450	                    "The app's registration on this server isn't valid, so sign-in \
451	                     can't continue. Nothing was granted. The app's developer needs to \
452	                     fix its registration.",
453	                )
454	                .into_response()
455	            }
456	            Err(ClientValidationError::InvalidRedirectUri) => {
457	                return error_page(
458	                    "Can't return you to the app",
459	                    "The app asked to send you to an address it hasn't registered, so \
460	                     you weren't sent anywhere and nothing was granted. If this keeps \
461	                     happening, tell the app's developer.",
462	                )
463	                .into_response()
464	            }
465	        };
466	
467	    // From here on redirect_uri is validated — errors redirect there, not to an error page.
468	    if params.response_type != "code" {
469	        return error_redirect(
470	            &params.redirect_uri,
471	            "unsupported_response_type",
472	            "only response_type=code is supported",
473	            &params.state,
474	            &issuer,
475	            params.response_mode,
476	        )
477	        .into_response();
478	    }
479	
480	    if params.code_challenge_method != "S256" {
481	        return error_redirect(
482	            &params.redirect_uri,
483	            "invalid_request",
484	            "code_challenge_method must be S256",
485	            &params.state,
486	            &issuer,
487	            params.response_mode,
488	        )
489	        .into_response();
490	    }
491	
492	    let client_name = metadata
493	        .client_name
494	        .unwrap_or_else(|| params.client_id.clone());
495	
496	    // Render-only expansion: shows the user real permissions instead of an opaque `include:`
497	    // reference. `post_authorization` re-runs expansion authoritatively regardless of what's
498	    // rendered here (hidden form fields are attacker-controllable), but a resolution failure
499	    // still redirects with an error rather than falling back to the raw unexpanded scope: if the
500	    // page fell back and a transient failure then cleared before the user submits,
501	    // `post_authorization`'s authoritative expansion would produce granular tokens that don't
502	    // match the raw `include:<nsid>` checkbox value the page rendered, and the grant-reduction
503	    // filter would silently drop everything from that set — a real (if narrow) desync between
504	    // what the user saw/approved and what gets granted. Failing the page outright avoids that
505	    // class of bug entirely, at the cost of requiring a retry on a transient blip.
506	    let display_scope = match crate::auth::permission_sets::expand_include_scopes(
507	        &state,
508	        &state.permission_set_cache,
509	        &params.scope,
510	    )
511	    .await
512	    {
513	        Ok(s) => s,
514	        Err(desc) => {
515	            return error_redirect(
516	                &params.redirect_uri,
517	                "invalid_scope",
518	                &desc,
519	                &params.state,
520	                &issuer,
521	                params.response_mode,
522	            )
523	            .into_response()
524	        }
525	    };
526	
527	    // Wallet-confirmed consent path: create a single-use pending request that a sovereign /
528	    // passwordless account approves out-of-band from its wallet. This is best-effort — a creation
529	    // failure (rate limit, DB error) simply degrades to the legacy password-only page rather than
530	    // breaking consent for passworded accounts.
531	    let wallet_codes = create_pending_request(
532	        &state,
533	        &headers,
534	        &params,
535	        client_name.as_str(),
536	        &display_scope,
537	    )
538	    .await;
539	    let wallet = wallet_codes.as_ref().map(|pending| WalletConsentPath {
540	        user_code: &pending.user_code,
541	        request_id: &pending.request_id,
542	        origin: pending.origin.as_deref(),
543	        match_code: pending.match_code.as_deref(),
544	    });
545	
546	    Html(render_consent_page(
547	        &client_name,
548	        &params.client_id,
549	        &params.redirect_uri,
550	        &params.code_challenge,
551	        &params.code_challenge_method,
552	        &params.state,
553	        &display_scope,
554	        &params.response_type,
555	        params.response_mode,
556	        &state.config.public_url,
557	        params.login_hint.as_deref(),
558	        None,
559	        wallet.as_ref(),
560	    ))
561	    .into_response()
562	}

564	/// What `create_pending_request` hands the consent page to render: the typed code, the poll /
565	/// handoff key, the snapshotted origin, and — when a `login-approval` push went out — the
566	/// number-match code the page must display (V060).
567	struct PendingWalletRequest {
568	    user_code: String,
569	    request_id: String,
570	    origin: Option<String>,
571	    match_code: Option<String>,
572	}
573	
574	/// Create a single-use pending wallet-consent request, returning what the page renders (the
575	/// origin is snapshotted into the scan QR alongside the request_id), or `None` if creation should
576	/// be skipped (rate limited or a DB error) — the caller degrades to the password-only page.
577	/// Snapshots the client metadata and requesting context so the wallet preview and later
578	/// completion never re-resolve the client document, and audits the creation. When the request's
579	/// `login_hint` names a local account, a sealed `login-approval` push is dispatched to that
580	/// account's registered wallet devices (Phase C).
581	async fn create_pending_request(
582	    state: &AppState,
583	    headers: &HeaderMap,
584	    params: &AuthorizeQuery,
585	    client_name: &str,
586	    display_scope: &str,
587	) -> Option<PendingWalletRequest> {
588	    let client_ip = crate::rate_limit::client_ip_from_headers(headers);
589	    if state
590	        .rate_limiter
591	        .check_oauth_consent_creation(&params.client_id, &client_ip)
592	        .is_err()
593	    {
594	        tracing::debug!(client_id = %params.client_id, "wallet-consent request creation rate-limited");
595	        return None;
596	    }
597	
598	    let header_str = |name: &str| {
599	        headers
600	            .get(name)
601	            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
602	            .map(str::to_string)
603	    };
604	    // Keep only scheme + host (+ port) from Origin/Referer — never a full referring URL's path or
605	    // query — in the pending row and audit log.
606	    let origin = header_str("origin")
607	        .or_else(|| header_str("referer"))
608	        .and_then(|raw| sanitize_origin(&raw));
609	    let user_agent = header_str("user-agent");
610	
611	    let request_id = format!("poauth_{}", generate_token().plaintext);
612	    let user_code = generate_login_code();
613	
614	    // Reclaim long-expired rows before inserting (the oauth_par_requests / transfers precedent),
615	    // so the table stays bounded without a background sweep.
616	    if cleanup_expired_pending_authorizations(&state.db, PENDING_REQUEST_CLEANUP_GRACE_SECS)
617	        .await
618	        .is_err()
619	    {
620	        return None;
621	    }
622	
623	    let new = NewPendingOAuthAuthorization {
624	        request_id: &request_id,
625	        user_code: &user_code,
626	        client_id: &params.client_id,
627	        client_name: Some(client_name),
628	        redirect_uri: &params.redirect_uri,
629	        code_challenge: &params.code_challenge,
630	        code_challenge_method: &params.code_challenge_method,
631	        state: &params.state,
632	        response_type: &params.response_type,
633	        response_mode: params.response_mode.as_str(),
634	        requested_scope: display_scope,
635	        login_hint: params.login_hint.as_deref(),
636	        origin: origin.as_deref(),
637	        ip: Some(client_ip.as_str()),
638	        user_agent: user_agent.as_deref(),
639	        dpop_jkt: params.dpop_jkt.as_deref(),
640	        ttl_secs: PENDING_REQUEST_TTL_SECS,
641	    };
642	    if insert_pending_authorization(&state.db, &new).await.is_err() {
643	        return None;
644	    }
645	
646	    // Audit the creation (best-effort — a failed audit must not deny the consent page). The
647	    // account_did is left NULL here: the client-supplied login_hint is unverified (it can be a
648	    // handle or an attacker-chosen DID), so it is recorded as a mechanical `login_hint` fact in the
649	    // detail rather than attributed as the approving account — that binding is only established at
650	    // approval, against authoritative PLC state.
651	    let detail = serde_json::json!({
652	        "client_id": params.client_id,
653	        "requested_scope": display_scope,
654	        "origin": origin,
655	        "login_hint": params.login_hint,
656	    })
657	    .to_string();
658	    if let Err(e) = insert_oauth_consent_audit_event(
659	        &state.db,
660	        &uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
661	        &request_id,
662	        None,
663	        &params.client_id,
664	        OAuthConsentAuditEventType::RequestCreated,
665	        Some(&detail),
666	    )
667	    .await
668	    {
669	        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to audit wallet-consent request creation");
670	    }
671	
672	    // Phase C: push-to-approve. Best-effort — a push is a convenience layer on the same pending
673	    // request, and every failure here degrades to the Phase A/B channels (typed code, QR,
674	    // handoff) already rendered on the page.
675	    let match_code = dispatch_login_approval_push(
676	        state,
677	        &request_id,
678	        &params.client_id,
679	        client_name,
680	        origin.as_deref(),
681	        params.login_hint.as_deref(),
682	    )
683	    .await;
684	
685	    Some(PendingWalletRequest {
686	        user_code,
687	        request_id,
688	        origin,
689	        match_code,
690	    })
691	}

693	/// Resolve a client-supplied `login_hint` to a local, active account DID — **local lookups
694	/// only**. This runs on an unauthenticated surface with an attacker-suppliable hint, so it must
695	/// never drive outbound handle resolution (the SSRF/amplification posture); an account not on
696	/// this instance has no registered wallet devices to push to anyway.
697	async fn resolve_login_hint_to_local_did(state: &AppState, hint: &str) -> Option<String> {
698	    let did = if hint.starts_with("did:") {
699	        hint.to_string()
700	    } else {
701	        let handle = hint.strip_prefix("at://").unwrap_or(hint);
702	        let handle = handle
703	            .strip_prefix('@')
704	            .unwrap_or(handle)
705	            .to_ascii_lowercase();
706	        crate::identity::handle::validate_handle_structure(&handle).ok()?;
707	        crate::db::handles::resolve_handle(&state.db, &handle)
708	            .await
709	            .ok()??
710	    };
711	    match active_local_account_exists(&state.db, &did).await {
712	        Ok(true) => Some(did),
713	        _ => None,
714	    }
715	}
716	
717	/// Seal and enqueue a `login-approval` push toward the hinted account's registered wallet
718	/// devices, then latch the number-match requirement onto the pending row. Returns the two-digit
719	/// match code for the page to display, or `None` when no push went out.
720	///
721	/// Anyone can type a victim's handle into a consent page, so this channel is exactly where
722	/// MFA-fatigue / blind-tap attacks live. Two mitigations gate it: creation is rate-limited per
723	/// client and per IP (`check_oauth_consent_creation`, upstream of this call), and once a push is
724	/// dispatched approval REQUIRES the number displayed on the login surface — a victim who is not
725	/// looking at any sign-in page has nothing to type. The payload is HPKE-sealed to each device and
726	/// the relay sees only an opaque push handle, so the relay never learns a login is happening.
727	async fn dispatch_login_approval_push(
728	    state: &AppState,
729	    request_id: &str,
730	    client_id: &str,
731	    client_name: &str,
732	    origin: Option<&str>,
733	    login_hint: Option<&str>,
734	) -> Option<String> {
735	    // Cheap outs before any lookup: no relay configured, or no hint to name a recipient.
736	    state.notify_sender.as_ref()?;
737	    let did = resolve_login_hint_to_local_did(state, login_hint?).await?;
738	
739	    // The number is deliberately absent from the payload: it is the proof the approver can see
740	    // the login surface, so handing it to the wallet would defeat the channel binding. The wallet
741	    // re-fetches everything it displays from the server's record by `request_id` (the QR-path
742	    // discipline); `clientName`/`origin` ride along only for the banner the NSE renders.
743	    let body = match origin {
744	        Some(origin) => format!(
745	            "{client_name} at {origin} is asking to sign in as you. If this is you, open the \
746	             request and enter the number shown on the sign-in screen."
747	        ),
748	        None => format!(
749	            "{client_name} is asking to sign in as you. If this is you, open the request and \
750	             enter the number shown on the sign-in screen."
751	        ),
752	    };
753	    let payload = NotificationPayload::new("login-approval", "Sign-in request", body).with_data(
754	        serde_json::json!({
755	            "requestId": request_id,
756	            "did": did,
757	            "clientName": client_name,
758	            "origin": origin,
759	        }),
760	    );
761	    let enqueued = notify_device(state, &did, payload).await;
762	    if enqueued == 0 {
763	        return None;
764	    }
765	
766	    // Latch the requirement only after at least one sealed payload was enqueued: matching is
767	    // mandatory on the push channel, and requiring a number no push ever announced would add
768	    // friction to the wallet-initiated channels for nothing.
769	    let match_code = generate_match_code();
770	    match set_push_dispatched(&state.db, request_id, &match_code).await {
771	        Ok(true) => {}
772	        Ok(false) => {
773	            tracing::warn!(request_id = %request_id, "push dispatched but the match code did not latch");
774	            return None;
775	        }
776	        Err(e) => {
777	            tracing::warn!(error = %e, request_id = %request_id, "failed to record push dispatch");
778	            return None;
779	        }
780	    }
781	
782	    // `account_did` stays NULL like the creation event — that column means "the approving
783	    // account", a binding only established at approval. The push target is a mechanical fact.
784	    let detail = serde_json::json!({ "devices": enqueued, "pushed_to": did }).to_string();
785	    if let Err(e) = insert_oauth_consent_audit_event(
786	        &state.db,
787	        &uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
788	        request_id,
789	        None,
790	        client_id,
791	        OAuthConsentAuditEventType::PushDispatched,
792	        Some(&detail),
793	    )
794	    .await
795	    {
796	        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to audit login-approval push dispatch");
797	    }
798	
799	    Some(match_code)
800	}

# PDS Crate (Custos)

Last verified: 2026-08-02

## Purpose

The PDS is the axum-based web server. It is the sole Imperative Shell in the workspace —
the only crate that touches SQLite, handles HTTP, or manages process-level state. All other
crates (`crypto`, `repo-engine`, `common`) are pure Functional Cores that the PDS calls.

This file is a map. Each entry is what the module is plus the fact or two an agent needs
before opening it; mechanism and invariants live in the module's own `//!` doc.

## Module Map

### `firehose/`

The persistent event pipeline behind `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`: a durable monotonic
sequencer (`repo_seq`, V028) plus a Tokio broadcast fan-out, shared as `AppState.firehose`.
Three files — `mod.rs` (sequencer, bare `emit_*` primitives, and the staged-transaction path
`lock_emit`/`EmitGuard`/`Pending*`), `events.rs` (wire-facing event model + DAG-CBOR stored
encoding), `replay.rs` (cursor replay over the durable log) — with every public type
re-exported at `crate::firehose::*`. The invariants that make it subtle (persist-before-
broadcast under one `emit_lock`, the lock-before-transaction deadlock rule on this crate's
single-connection pool, staging into a caller's transaction, cancellation recovery via
`insert_at_frontier`, and the emission map of which routes emit which frames) are documented
in `firehose/mod.rs`'s module and item docs — read those before touching any emit path.

### `crawler.rs`

Outbound `com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl` notifier (`AppState.crawlers`). Fires on startup and on
**every** firehose broadcast frame — lifecycle frames included, so a relay that silently dropped
its subscription is re-invited even when the only news is a post-migration `#account`/`#sync`.
Fire-and-forget, rate-limited to one notification per crawler per 30s, retried with backoff;
configured via `[crawlers] urls` / `EZPDS_CRAWLERS` (default `["https://bsky.network"]`, empty
disables). Mechanism and invariants: the module doc in `src/crawler.rs`.

### `relay_status.rs`

The inbound half of federation health: a `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` client asking the
upstream relay what it knows about this PDS, backing `GET /v1/admin/relay-status` (which compares
the relay's cursor against our exact sequencer head — see that route's row below, and
`admin_request_crawl.rs` for the companion action). Total, never fatal: every failure becomes a
`RelayReport` variant, so the readout always renders the outcome — what the relay said, or that
it could not be asked. Details: the module doc in `src/relay_status.rs`.

### `rate_limit.rs`

Reference-parity request rate limiting. The pure sliding-window algorithm lives in
`auth/rate_limit.rs` (Functional Core); this module is the Imperative Shell owning the
process-level limiters and the Axum middleware. Three families — global per-IP, per-endpoint
per-IP (guess-target endpoint pairs share one limiter instance so alternating endpoints can't
double a guess budget), and per-account write points charged in `record_write::commit_repo_write`
on the **authenticated** DID — all off when `[rate_limit] enabled = false`, all tunable via
`[rate_limit]` / `EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_*` (a knob of `0` disables that limiter). The family
rosters, exemptions, and `RateLimit-*` header behavior: the module doc.

validation, the live signing-authority lookup behind the passwordless surfaces, and did:plc

`app.rs`/`xrpc_dispatch.rs`, and `main.rs`; a few also share helpers within the module (for
example `authority.rs` reads through `plc.rs` and `resolution.rs`, and `well_known.rs` borrows
`did.rs`'s validator), so check a file's imports before assuming it stands alone.

## Metrics

`GET /metrics` serves the federation-health instrument set. `metrics::names` in
`src/metrics.rs` is the single source of truth: each constant documents what it measures and
who records it, a unit test pins the rendered Prometheus names (counters gain their `_total`
suffix at export), and label values never come from request data. `GET /v1/admin/health`
mirrors the sweeps' last-run state as JSON via `sweep_status.rs`, so operators keep the
signal with `[telemetry] metrics_enabled` off.

## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. If it's an XRPC procedure: a JSON input body is parsed with `LexiconInput<T>` (never bare
   `axum::Json<T>`) after vendoring its lexicon document (`crates/pds/lexicons/README.md`); a
   no-input procedure takes `NoInputBody` instead. Both must be the handler's final extractor.
5. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
6. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root AGENTS.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

1. Identify the owning entity (`accounts`, `oauth`, etc.).
2. Add the function to the matching `db/<entity>.rs` file.
3. If no matching file exists, create one with `// pattern: Imperative Shell`.
4. Export the function and any new data struct via `db/mod.rs` (`pub mod <entity>;`).

Removing it would tighten things but adds a lot of diff surface for tests and docs, so I'm weighing whether it's worth it, and now I want to check how this interacts with the wallet/consent path.

The consent approval route reads pending rows separately and isn't affected. The wallet's own client behavior when acting as a PAR client against other servers is irrelevant here, but I need to confirm the wallet doesn't drive our authorize endpoint in some way that bypasses PAR—since GET now requires PAR, any consent page reached via GET will go through that path, which matches how real clients like official apps already behave.

I'm deciding to keep the live-resolution branch rather than remove it, since it still guards the POST side and removal can be a separate cleanup later. But the module doc claiming non-PAR clients still work is now inaccurate and needs updating to reflect that the branch is just a POST-leg safety net, and the GET-focused live-resolution tests will need to be reworked or removed since GET can no longer reach that code path.

I'm thinking through how to preserve test coverage—since the shared lookup_and_validate_client function is used by both GET and POST, I can't easily split it, so instead I'll rewrite the three live-resolution tests to exercise the branch via POST requests with unregistered client IDs. I also realize there's no new security exposure here since an attacker could already trigger arbitrary URL fetches through the unauthenticated /oauth/par endpoint, so keeping live resolution is fine. 13	**Reusable harness facts** (from `tools/mcp/test/harness.ts` — an established shared seam; mcp-sidecar imports it via relative path too):
14	- `spawnPds({dir, plcUrl, agentAuthEnabled})` configures the PDS purely via an **env allowlist** (`EZPDS_*`), nothing inherited but PATH. A `pds.toml` dropped in `dir` reaches settings with no env override.
15	- **The PDS refuses a non-https `public_url`**, so each instance is fronted by a loopback TLS proxy. The cert must exist before Node starts (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is read at startup only) → hence the two-stage `test/run.ts` wrapper. `harness.ts` hard-fails if `CUSTOS_MCP_TEST_TLS_DIR` is unset.
16	- `startMockPlc()` returns `{url, close}` (**`close`, not `stop`**) and answers every path `{}`.
17	- Account provisioning goes through `tools/interop`, whose config module **reads `EZPDS_BASE_URL` at first import and caches it** → **one fixture per test file**.
18	- `TestAccount` omits `password`; `createAccount()`'s raw return has it. The consent form needs it.
19	
20	**Two consent paths, and this matters:** `oauth_consent.rs` is the *wallet/passwordless half*; there IS also a password form (`ConsentForm` in `oauth_authorize.rs` with `identifier`/`password`). The **password path touches no plc.directory**, so the `{}` mock stub suffices — that's why the suite avoids needing a richer mock plc or a JS port of the consent envelope. The wallet path would need both (golden vector: `test-vectors/oauth-consent-envelope-v1.json`).
21	
22	**Loopback client_ids work**: `auth/oauth_client_resolution.rs` allows plain-http for localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 and exempts them from the reverse-FQDN redirect rule — this is what makes a hermetic third-party-client harness possible. The suite serves its own client-metadata doc from a loopback http server.
23	
24	**Testing token expiry:** `oauth.access_token_ttl_secs` (default 900, env `EZPDS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECS`, validated 1–1800). `startFixture({accessTokenTtlSecs: 2})` writes a `pds.toml` into the spawn dir — the escape hatch for settings not in `spawnPds`'s closed env allowlist, so the shared harness stays untouched. Adding any config field means running `just docs-generate` or `docs-check` fails.
25	
26	**Gotchas:**
27	- `.gitignore` covered only `apps/*/node_modules` until this change added `tools/*/node_modules/` — a `git add -A` in a tools package committed 1948 files once.
28	- devenv ships pnpm 9 but CI pins 10.33.0; both write `lockfileVersion 9.0` so `--frozen-lockfile` is fine.
29	- **`just <recipe>` runs in the shell's cwd, not the worktree — hit this TWICE.** `cd /main-checkout && nix develop -c bash -c 'just <recipe>'` runs against the MAIN checkout: `docs-generate` reported PASS while the worktree stayed stale, and `audit` kept "failing" because it read the main checkout's `.cargo/audit.toml` without my new ignore. The `cd` at the *start* of the Bash call does not survive into `bash -c`. **The `cd <worktree> &&` must be inside the `bash -c` string**, and add `pwd &&` when a recipe result surprises you — that is what finally exposed it. Same family as the `--manifest-path` trap in [[reference_worktree_cargo_via_main_devenv]].
30	- `touch <path>` in a pre-clippy command **creates** the file if absent — running it from the main checkout left a stray empty `.rs` there.
31	
32	Discipline note: after writing assertions, **falsify one deliberately** and confirm it fails — a suite that can't fail is the exact trap that let five OAuth bugs ship green. Sibling: [[project-oauth-interop-audit]].

`tools/oauth-conformance/` (added 2026-08-03, branch `claude/oauth-atproto-failures-4ff55e`) drives full OAuth flows against a hermetic PDS. `just oauth-conformance-setup` once, then `just oauth-conformance-test`. Runs in ci.yml's PDS gate reusing the binary `just ci-pds` built.

**Reusable harness facts** (from `tools/mcp/test/harness.ts` — an established shared seam; mcp-sidecar imports it via relative path too):
- `spawnPds({dir, plcUrl, agentAuthEnabled})` configures the PDS purely via an **env allowlist** (`EZPDS_*`), nothing inherited but PATH. A `pds.toml` dropped in `dir` reaches settings with no env override.
- **The PDS refuses a non-https `public_url`**, so each instance is fronted by a loopback TLS proxy. The cert must exist before Node starts (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is read at startup only) → hence the two-stage `test/run.ts` wrapper. `harness.ts` hard-fails if `CUSTOS_MCP_TEST_TLS_DIR` is unset.
- `startMockPlc()` returns `{url, close}` (**`close`, not `stop`**) and answers every path `{}`.
- Account provisioning goes through `tools/interop`, whose config module **reads `EZPDS_BASE_URL` at first import and caches it** → **one fixture per test file**.
- `TestAccount` omits `password`; `createAccount()`'s raw return has it. The consent form needs it.

**Two consent paths, and this matters:** `oauth_consent.rs` is the *wallet/passwordless half*; there IS also a password form (`ConsentForm` in `oauth_authorize.rs` with `identifier`/`password`). The **password path touches no plc.directory**, so the `{}` mock stub suffices — that's why the suite avoids needing a richer mock plc or a JS port of the consent envelope. The wallet path would need both (golden vector: `test-vectors/oauth-consent-envelope-v1.json`).

**Loopback client_ids work**: `auth/oauth_client_resolution.rs` allows plain-http for localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 and exempts them from the reverse-FQDN redirect rule — this is what makes a hermetic third-party-client harness possible. The suite serves its own client-metadata doc from a loopback http server.

**Testing token expiry:** `oauth.access_token_ttl_secs` (default 900, env `EZPDS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECS`, validated 1–1800). `startFixture({accessTokenTtlSecs: 2})` writes a `pds.toml` into the spawn dir — the escape hatch for settings not in `spawnPds`'s closed env allowlist, so the shared harness stays untouched. Adding any config field means running `just docs-generate` or `docs-check` fails.

**Gotchas:**
- `.gitignore` covered only `apps/*/node_modules` until this change added `tools/*/node_modules/` — a `git add -A` in a tools package committed 1948 files once.
- devenv ships pnpm 9 but CI pins 10.33.0; both write `lockfileVersion 9.0` so `--frozen-lockfile` is fine.
- **`just <recipe>` runs in the shell's cwd, not the worktree — hit this TWICE.** `cd /main-checkout && nix develop -c bash -c 'just <recipe>'` runs against the MAIN checkout: `docs-generate` reported PASS while the worktree stayed stale, and `audit` kept "failing" because it read the main checkout's `.cargo/audit.toml` without my new ignore. The `cd` at the *start* of the Bash call does not survive into `bash -c`. **The `cd <worktree> &&` must be inside the `bash -c` string**, and add `pwd &&` when a recipe result surprises you — that is what finally exposed it. Same family as the `--manifest-path` trap in [[reference_worktree_cargo_via_main_devenv]].
- `touch <path>` in a pre-clippy command **creates** the file if absent — running it from the main checkout left a stray empty `.rs` there.

Discipline note: after writing assertions, **falsify one deliberately** and confirm it fails — a suite that can't fail is the exact trap that let five OAuth bugs ship green. Sibling: [[project-oauth-interop-audit]].

crates/pds/src/db/AGENTS.md:7:- **V062**: Adds nullable `dpop_jkt` TEXT to `oauth_authorization_codes` and `pending_oauth_authorizations` — the client's DPoP key thumbprint carried from the pushed authorization request through to the code it eventually yields (RFC 9449 §10), so an intercepted code cannot be redeemed by anyone else. The PAR endpoint resolves the key from a proof header (validated by `auth::dpop::validate_dpop_for_par` — same checks as the token endpoint **minus the server-nonce requirement**, since a PAR is a flow's first contact and the proof only asserts the client's own key) or from an explicit `dpop_jkt` parameter, requiring the two to agree when both arrive; the value rides `StoredPARParams` into the pending consent row and is stamped onto the code by `store_authorization_code`. The token endpoint enforces it in constant time when present. Deliberately **not** enforced on two paths: the direct (non-PAR) authorize flow, where a client has no authenticated channel to assert a key, and the password-consent POST, whose PAR row is already consumed by the GET that rendered the form — a hidden field is attacker-controllable, and a binding an attacker can omit is no binding. content.content:
# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a
  change has no Linear issue, use the pull request number (for example, `271`).
- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```

The CI gate requires a fragment when a pull request changes a deployable surface:

- server or shared runtime source under `crates/*/src/`, plus PDS runtime assets;
- either mobile app's frontend, native runtime source, static assets, or Tauri config;
- the public marketing site;
- the deployed MCP surfaces — the stdio Custos MCP server (`tools/mcp/src/`) and the
  credential-forwarding sidecar (`tools/mcp-sidecar/src/`, plus its image/config), which
  ships as a Railway service and re-exports the stdio server's tool surface;
- the notification relay's own image, entrypoint, and Railway config

  stripped, before the single-use PAR row is consumed.
- The authorize-side live client-metadata resolution branch is removed: its
  stated rationale was serving clients that skip PAR, which are now refused,
  so registration happens only at /oauth/par and authorize reads the cache.

Unit tests now drive the GET leg through stored PAR requests; conformance
coverage pins both rejections (deliberately falsified once to prove the tests
can fail). Wallet and consent paths are untouched — the wallet already PARs.

Sequencing gate from the issue: resolved as moot 2026-08-14 — pckt.blog's
PAR/legacy classification is frozen client-side and will never flip; their
legacy flow was already broken post-consent, so enforcement only makes the
failure loud and immediate at flow start.
